   Power to license - see Ohio R.C. 715.61
   Private investigators; security guard providers - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 4749
   Private police officers - see ADM.
244.06
   Display of emblem by law enforcement agencies - see GEN. OFF.
606.26
866.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Private investigation" means the conducting or making, for hire, of
any investigation for the purpose of obtaining evidence or testimony to be used
before investigating committees, boards of award or arbitration or in the trial
of civil or criminal cases, or for the purpose of obtaining information with
reference to any of the following matters:
      (1)   Crimes or wrongs done Or threatened;
      (2)   The identity, habits, conduct, movements, whereabouts,
affiliations, transactions, reputation, credibility, character or location of
any person;
      (3)   The cause of or responsibility for any libel or slander;
      (4)   The location or recovery of lost or stolen property;
      (5)   The cause or origin of or responsibility for fires, accidents or
injuries to real or personal property or strikes and labor difficulties.
   (b)   "Private investigator" means any person who engages in private
investigation for hire, whether self-employed or employed by a private
investigation agency.
   (c)   "Private investigation agency" means a person employing, in the
private investigation business, one or more private investigators.
   (d)   "Security guard" means any person, in uniform or otherwise, who, for
hire or reward, guards or protects any structure, premises, property or person
by patrolling on foot or in any vehicle upon any street or other public way or
public place in the City. The term includes any person who, for fire or reward,
is employed to guard, protect or maintain peace and order in or about any
structure, premises or property which is operated, maintained or conducted as a
dance hall, theater or other place of amusement, recreation or entertainment
frequented by the public, including liquor establishments licensed under State
statutes.
   (e)   "Security guard agency" means any person who or which employs,
furnishes or provides the service of a security guard.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.02 LICENSE REQUIRED; EMPLOYMENT OF UNLICENSED PERSONS OR AGENCIES.
   (a)   No person shall operate a private investigation agency or security
guard agency or act as a private investigator or security guard within the City
unless duly licensed as provided in this chapter.
   (b)   No person shall knowingly employ or hire the services of an unlicensed
private investigator, security guard, private investigation agency or security
guard agency.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.03 EXCEPTIONS.
   This chapter shall not apply to the following:
   (a)   Employment as regularly appointed police officers, regularly appointed
peace officers or law enforcement agents of the United States, the State or
political subdivisions thereof;
   (b)   Off-duty employment as regularly appointed police officers of the City
when approved by the Chief of Police or as regularly appointed members of the
County Sheriff's office when approved by the Sheriff;
   (c)   The protection of persons or property being transported in interstate
commerce;
   (d)   The investigation and adjustment of insurance losses;
   (e)   Attorneys at law in the practice of their profession;
   (f)   Agencies whose exclusive business is the furnishing of information as
to the business, financial standing and credit responsibility of persons, or
the personal habits and financial responsibility of applicants or claimants
with respect to insurance, indemnity bonds or commercial credit; or
   (g)   Employment as security guards in private business establishments,
premises or structures, where the major portion of such employment is confined
to services within such private business establishments, premises or
structures, and where such establishments, premises or structures are not
places of amusement, recreation, retail, discount or wholesale sales, or
entertainment, frequented by the public, including liquor establishments
licensed under State statutes.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.04 LICENSE APPLICATION; FINGERPRINTS AND PHOTOGRAPHS.
   Application for private investigation agency, private investigator, security
guard agency or security guard licenses shall be made to the Mayor on forms
approved by him or her. Applicants shall be fingerprinted and photographed by
the Police Division.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.05 LICENSE ISSUANCE.
   (a)   Licenses required by this chapter shall be issued only to persons who
are eighteen years of age or older. Licenses shall not be issued to persons who
have been adjudged insane, convicted of a felony or of a crime involving
violence or moral turpitude, or found, upon investigation, by the Chief of
Police, not to be of good character.
   (b)   Any person found, upon investigation by the Chief of Police, not to be
of good character, shall be entitled, upon request, to a copy of such adverse
finding.
   (c)   When the Mayor is satisfied that there is a necessity therefor and
that the applicant is of good moral character, competency and integrity and has
complied with all of the requirements of this chapter, then, upon payment of
the proper license fee, the Mayor's office shall issue the license applied for.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.06 LICENSE FEES; FORM; DISPLAY.
   (a)   All licenses granted under this chapter shall expire in one year,
unless sooner revoked. The following fees shall be collected by the Mayor:
      (1)   For a private investigator or security guard, fifty dollars
($50.00);
      (2)   For a private investigation agency or security guard agency, one
hundred dollars ($100.00).
   (b)   The license for a private investigator or security guard shall be in
such form as to contain a true photograph and right thumbprint of the licensee
and his or her name, address, physical description and signature. Such license
shall be carried by the licensee during his or her hours of employment or duty
and shall be subject at all times to inspection by any member of the Police
Division.
   (c)   The license for a private investigation agency or security guard
agency shall be in a form prescribed by the Mayor and shall be displayed at the
licensee's office.
   (d)   Fees collected under this section shall be deposited into the General
Fund of the City.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.07 BOND AND INSURANCE.
   (a)   Each applicant for a license under this chapter shall file with the
Mayor's office an approved fidelity bond in the principal sum of ten thousand
dollars ($10,000), in favor of the City, for the benefit of any person damaged
by a dishonest or fraudulent act of the applicant. Such bond shall be
maintained in full force and in the full principal amount at all times and
shall provide that it shall not be cancelled or revoked until ten days after
written notice of intention to cancel or revoke has been given to the Mayor's
office.
   (b)   In addition to the bond required in subsection (a) hereof, each
applicant shall file with the Mayor's office an approved policy of public
liability insurance, including coverage for false arrest, having coverage
limits of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) per person, one hundred thousand
dollars ($100,000) per accident and twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) for
property damage. Such policy of insurance shall be maintained in full force and
full coverage at all times and shall provide that it shall not be cancelled or
revoked until ten days after written notice of intention to cancel or revoke
has been given to the Mayor's office.
   (c)   The insolvency or bankruptcy of a licensee shall not operate to
release a surety or insurer from liability upon a bond or policy of insurance.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.08 LICENSE SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION.
   The Mayor is hereby authorized to suspend or revoke any license granted
under this chapter and to refuse to grant or renew any license to any person
who violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this chapter,
after first giving the licensee an opportunity to be heard. Sikh suspensions
and revocations shall be in addition to the penalty provided in Section
866.99.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.09 REPORTS FILED WITH POLICE CHIEF.
   (a)   Every private investigation agency and security guard agency licensed
under this chapter shall immediately submit to the Chief of Police, in writing,
the names of all persons in its employ and thereafter the names of all persons
hired or discharged.
   (b)   Licensees shall report all police action taken, except routine patrol
duty, to the Chief of Police within twelve hours and shall report as soon as
practical to the Chief of Police all property found or recovered.
   (c)   Licensees shall report all knowledge or information of any crime to
the Division of Police.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.10 UNIFORMS AND BADGES.
   (a)   Licensed security guards may wear a uniform and a badge of a design
approved by the Chief of Police, which design shall substantially differ from
those worn by members of the Division of Police.
   (b)   Licensed private investigators may carry badges approved by the Chief
of Police, the design of which shall differ substantially from that worn by
members of the Division of Police.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.11 VEHICLES.
   Licensees under this chapter may identify vehicles used by them while on
patrol, but only in a manner approved by the Chief of Police.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.12 RADIOS.
   Vehicles equipped with radios capable of being tuned to the City police
frequency shall not be used without the knowledge of the Chief of Police.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.13 OATH.
   Upon issuance of a license under this chapter, the licensee shall take and
subscribe to an oath or affirmation similar to that administered to police
officers of the City.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.14 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Mayor is hereby authorized to promulgate rules and regulations, not
inconsistent with this chapter or with State law, for the administration and
enforcement of this chapter. No person shall violate or fail to comply with any
such rule or regulation.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
866.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree and shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty
days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)

CHAPTER 872
Secondhand Dealers
872.01   Secondhand dealer defined.
872.02   License required; application.
872.03   Effective period; fee; form; transferability; display.
872.04   Licensee's bond.
872.05   Record book; inspection; information form.
872.06   Daily report.
872.07   Tag on purchases.
872.08   Removing articles before thirty days.
872.09   Purchases from drunkards or thieves.
872.10   Purchases from minors; hours of operation.
872.11   Exceptions.
872.12   Revocation of license.
 
872.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Power to regulate - see Ohio R.C. 715.61
   Revocation of licenses of convicts - see Ohio R.C. 2961.03
   Secondhand dealers - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 4737
   Receiving stolen property - see GEN. OFF.
642.22 
   Pawnbrokers and dealers in precious metals - see B.R. & T. Ch.
860
872.01 SECONDHAND DEALER DEFINED.
   As used in this chapter, "secondhand dealer" means any person dealing in the
purchase or sale of secondhand articles of whatever nature, other than old
gold, silver, platinum or other precious metal Or jewels of any description and
other than secondhand manufactured articles composed wholly or in part of gold,
silver, platinum or other precious metal or jewels of any description, or in
the purchase or sale of pawnbroker tickets or other evidence of pledged
articles or, not being a person licensed under Chapter
860, any person ' dealing in the redemption or sale of furs, clothing or other
pledged articles.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.02 LICENSE REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   No secondhand dealer shall engage in the business of keeping a secondhand
store or a place for buying and selling secondhand goods in the City until he
or she has first obtained a license to engage in and carry on such business.
Every applicant for a license shall make application in writing to the Chief of
Police, which application shall set forth the name under which the business is
to be conducted, the name of every person interested in the business and the
location at which the business is to be conducted. The application must be made
by the person who is to conduct the business and must contain references of at
least two other residents of the City as to the character of the applicant.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.03 EFFECTIVE PERIOD; FEE; FORM; TRANSFERABILITY; DISPLAY.
   Licenses required by this chapter shall be issued annually and shall expire
annually on December 31. The license fee shall be fifty dollars ($50.00) per
year. The license shall contain the name under which the business is to be
conducted, the name of every person interested in the business and the location
at which the business is to be conducted. Licenses issued under this chapter
shall not be transferable to any other person. The business may be conducted
only at the location for which the license is issued and the license must be
conspicuously displayed.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.04 LICENSEE'S BOND.
   Every person licensed under this chapter shall execute and file a bond in
the sum of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500), with a surety to the
satisfaction of the Director of Law, conditioned upon such person's conforming
to the requirements of law and the ordinances of the City.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.05 RECORD BOOK; INSPECTION; INFORMATION FORM.
   Every person licensed under this chapter shall keep a book in which shall be
written in ink in the English language at the time of the purchase of any
secondhand article, a description thereof and the price paid the seller
therefor, together with a statement of the age, address and personal
description of the person from whom such purchase was made and the date and
hour of such purchase, which statement shall be signed in the book by the
seller. Such book shall at all times be open to the inspection of any member of
the Police Division. In addition to such book every person so licensed shall,
at the time of such purchase, fill out on a blank to be furnished by the Police
Division, such information as may be called for by the blank form, and on the
back of the blank forth the seller shall write, in his or her own handwriting,
his or her name, age and address. No entry in such book or on such form shall
be erased, obliterated, altered or defaced.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.06 DAILY REPORT.
   Every person licensed under this chapter shall, on every weekday before the
hour of 12:00 noon, make out a report ova a blank form, to be furnished by the
Police Division for that purpose, including a legible and correct copy of the
record required to be kept, containing all the particulais of all purchases of
articles made on the preceding business day, and shall deliver such report to
the Chief of Police or to his or her authorized representative, together with
the blanks furnished by the Police Division, properly completed and signed by
the seller, in accordance with the provisions of Section
872.05, or the report and completed blank may, if the Chief of Police so
elects, be mailed to such address as the Chief of Police may designate in
writing.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-8'.)
872.07 TAG ON PURCHASES.
   Every person licensed under this chapter shall, at the time of making any
purchase as aforesaid, attach a tag with a designating number thereon, legibly
written in the English language, to each article purchased, and shall make an
entry of such number in the book provided for in Section
872.05.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.08 REMOVING ARTICLES BEFORE THIRTY DAYS.
   No person licensed under this chapter shall sell or remove from his or her
place of business any secondhand goods, articles or things sold to him or her
until the same have been in his or her possession at least thirty days, except
as otherwise provided in Ohio R.C. 4737.02.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.09 PURCHASES FROM DRUNKARDS OR THIEVES.
   No person licensed under this chapter shall purchase any secondhand goods,
articles or things from any person who is at the time intoxicated, from an
habitual drunkard, from any person known by him or her to be a thief or an
associate of thieves, from any receiver of stolen property or from any person
he or she has reason to suspect to be a receiver of stolen property.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.10 PURCHASES FROM MINORS; HOURS OF OPERATION.
   No person shall receive, by sale, barter, exchange or otherwise, any article
mentioned in this chapter from a minor under the age of eighteen years, knowing
or having reason to believe him or her to be such, nor from any person between
the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. of the following day, prevailing time.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.11 EXCEPTIONS.
   This chapter shall not apply to persons who deal exclusively in furniture,
nor to persons who deal exclusively in secondhand automobiles. Nothing
contained in this chapter shall be construed to apply to pianos, books,
magazines, rugs, tapestries, burlap, paintings, drawings, etchings or
engravings.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.12 REVOCATION OF LICENSE.
   The Director of Safety may revoke the license of any person licensed under
this chapter who is found guilty of violating or failing to comply with any of
the provisions hereof. Any person whose license is revoked shall not be issued
another license before the expiration of one year from the date of the
revocation.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
872.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree and shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty
days, or both. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or
on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
CHAPTER 874
Shopping Carts
874.01   Definitions.
874.02   Identification of carts.
874.03   Removal from business establishments.
874.04   Removal from public places.
874.05   Redemption of carts.
874.06   Sale of carts at public auction.
874.07   Disposition of carts.
874.08   Disposition of proceeds.
874.09   Application of chapter.
 
874.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Criminal damaging or endangering - see GEN. OFF.
642.10 
   Criminal mischief - see OEN. OFF.
642.11
   Conduct in shopping centers - see GEN. OFF.
648.13
874.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Shopping cart" means either a hand drawn or rolling vehicle or a
nonrolling basket or container, made of wire, metal, wood or other material,
such as are generally provided by merchants for carting or carrying merchandise
of any kind from within a building to automobiles.
   (b)   "Public place" means and includes a street, sidewalk, avenue, road,
alley, lane, highway and curb lane
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.02 IDENTIFICATION OF CARTS.
   Every person who, by reason of his, her or its business establishment and
procedure, makes shopping carts available to the public, shall conspicuously
identify such carts with an identification clearly indicating the name of the
person or establishment and the location of the same.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.03 REMOVAL FROM BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS.
   No person shall remove a shopping cart from the property or the adjacent
parking lot of any business establishment.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.04 REMOVAL FROM PUBLIC PLACES.
   The Department of Service may remove any shopping cart found in a public
place, storing the same in a place of safekeeping in the City until it is
redeemed, sold or otherwise disposed of as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.05 REDEMPTION OF CARTS.
   Whenever the City removes any cart bearing identification of ownership, the
Department of Service shall mail a notice to the owner at the location shown on
such cart. Such notice shall advise that carts may be redeemed upon payment of
ten dollars ($10.00) to the Department of Finance for each cart to be redeemed
and shall set forth the place for redemption of carts and the place where
possession of the same may be had. Payment for redemption shall be made to the
Department of Finance and a receipt shall be given therefor, which receipt
shall entitle the owner to redeem, at the place of storage thereof, one or more
carts, as provided for in the receipt, upon surrender of the same at the place
of storage of the carts. No cart shall be delivered to a person seeking to
redeem the same unless proof of such person's ownership or right to possession
is submitted to the City. Such proof shall be to the satisfaction of the City.
Any delivery to a person deemed entitled thereto by the City, from the proof
submitted, shall be an absolute defense of the City against any other person
claiming to be entitled thereto.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.06 SALE OF CARTS AT PUBLIC AUCTION.
   After the mailing of the notice provided for in Section
874.05, or after removal of a cart bearing no identification of ownership, the
City shall from time to time sell such carts at public auction. Notice of such
public auction shall be given by publication in a newspaper of general
circulation in the City at least once, the first date of publication to be not
less than ten days prior to the date of public auction. Such notice shall set
forth the time and place of holding such public auction and shall also advise
that such carts will be sold at public auction for not less than fifteen
dollars ($15.00) each. Carts may be redeemed by the owner thereof at least two
days prior to such public auction upon payment to the City of ten dollars
($10.00) for each cart. No cart shall be delivered to a person seeking to
redeem the same unless proof of such person's ownership or right to possession
is submitted to the City. Such proof shall be to the satisfaction of the City.
Any delivery to a person deemed entitled thereto by the City, from the proof
subMitted, shall be an absolute defense of the City against any other person
claiming to be entitled thereto.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.07 DISPOSITION OF CARTS.
   If a cart is not sold at public auction, the City may similarly offer the
same again for public auction or dismantle, destroy or otherwise dispose of
such cart. Any disposition of a cart made pursuant to this chapter shall be
without liability of the City to any person lawfully entitled thereto or having
an interest therein.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.08 DISPOSITION OF PROCEEDS.
   Upon redemption or sale of a cart, the proceeds thereof shall be deposited
into the General Fund of the City.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.09 APPLICATION OF CHAPTER
   This chapter shall apply to any cart or personal property which may come
into the possession or custody of any department of the City pursuant to any
other ordinance or regulation.
(Ord. 1971-219. Passed 9-15-71.)
874.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00) for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed
committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or
continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
CHAPTER 876
Snow Removal Vehicles
876.01   Snow removal vehicle defined.
876.02   Permit required; application; fee; insurance; display.
876.03   Disposal of snow; emergency flashers required.
 
876.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Snow removal emergencies and contracts - see Ohio R.C. 505.82
   Snow removal equipment - see Ohio R.C. 505.82, 4513.18
   Snow removal - see Ohio R.C. 505.82, 5501.41, 5571.08
   Placing injurious material or obstruction in street - see TRAF.
412.01
   Commercial and heavy vehicles - see TRAF. Chs.
440,
442 
   Parking during snow emergencies - see TRAF.

876.01 SNOW REMOVAL VEHICLE DEFINED.
   As used in this chapter, "snow removal vehicle" means any type of vehicle
which is authorized and licensed by the State or by any other state,
authorizing such vehicle to be operated on public streets.
(Ord. 1972-196. Passed 10-18-72; Ord. 2008-127. Passed 12-17-08.)
876.02 PERMIT REQUIRED; APPLICATION; FEE; INSURANCE; DISPLAY.
   (a)   No person shall use a vehicle as a snow removal vehicle on any public
streets or private property in the City without first obtaining a permit.
Application for such a permit shall be made to the Director of Service on forms
furnished by the Service Department. The fee for such a permit shall be twenty
dollars ($20.00). Such permits shall be effective for a period of one year from
the date of the issuance.
   (b)   In addition to other requirements, the applicant must show proof of a
commercial liability insurance covering the vehicle for which a permit is
applied for in amounts not less than are prescribed by the financial security
laws of the State. Such proof must be offered prior to the issuance of the
permit applied for.
(Ord. 1996-24. Passed 3-6-96.)
   (c)   Upon issuance, the permit shall be conspicuously displayed and visible
from the exterior of the snow removal vehicle.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87; Ord. 2008-127. Passed 12-17-08.)
876.03 DISPOSAL OF SNOW; EMERGENCY FLASHERS REQUIRED.
   (a)   Snow removed from any driveway, parking lot or sidewalk, either public
or private, shall be disposed of on the lot or parcel from which the same was
removed, or on the tree lawn immediately in front of such lot or parcel, in
such a manner so as to permit a person to see over the piles of snow, when such
person is either driving into or backing out of the driveway of the premises,
or to see around corners. No person shall pile snow, within 15 feet of the
intersection of any street or other public way, or within 15 feet of any
entrance to or exit from any premises.
   (b)   Snow removal equipment shall be illuminated with emergency flashers as
provided by the laws of the State.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87; Ord. 2008-127. Passed 12-17-08.)
876.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) for each offense. A separate offense shall be
deemed committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance
occurs or continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87; Ord. 2008-127. Passed 12-17-08.)

CHAPTER 880
Tanning Facilities
880.01   Definitions.
880.02   Permit required; fee; expiration; transfers.
880.03   Compliance with State law.

880.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter, "tanning facility" means a room or a booth which
houses ultraviolet lamps or products containing such lamps intended for the
irradiation of any part of the living human body for cosmetic or nonmedical
related purposes.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
880.02 PERMIT REQUIRED; FEE; EXPIRATION; TRANSFERS.
   No person shall own or operate a tanning facility in the City without first
obtaining a permit therefor as provided herein. Applications for such permits
shall be made to the Mayor on forms provided by him or her. The fee for such a
permit is twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per year or any part of a year and all
such permits shall expire on December 31 of the year of issuance. Such permits
shall not be transferable.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
880.03 COMPLIANCE WITH STATE LAW.
   The Mayor shall not issue a permit required by Section
880.01 until the applicant therefor submits to the Mayor, as part of his or her
application for the permit, proof of compliance with Ohio R.C. 4713.25 and the
rules and regulations of the Ohio State Board of Cosmetology promulgated
pursuant thereto. Further, no person shall own or operate a tanning facility
without being at all times in compliance with Ohio R.C. 4713.25 and such rules
and regulations.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
880.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree and shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty
days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deenied committed
each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
CHAPTER 882
Taxicabs
882.01    Taxicab defined.
882.02   Vehicle license required; expiration; fees.
882.03   License application; issuance.
882.04    Insurance or other security.
882.05   Taxicab stands.
882.06   Display of rates; overcharging.
882.07   Age limit for drivers.
882.08   Suspension and revocation of vehicle license.
882.09   Renewal of vehicle license.
 
882.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Operation of motor vehicles - see TRAF. Ch.
432 
   Vehicle equipment - see TRAF. Ch.
438
   Taxicab stands - see TRAF.
452.10
882.01 TAXICAB DEFINED.
   As used in this chapter, "taxicab" means any vehicle whose owner or driver
solicits, secures or accepts passengers for hire upon hail or request on the
public streets in the City.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.02 VEHICLE LICENSE REQUIRED; EXPIRATION; FEES.
   No person shall operate or cause to be operated a taxicab, or proffer the
services of any vehicle as a taxicab, unless the owner of such vehicle has
obtained a taxicab license, as provided in this chapter, covering such vehicle.
   Every such taxicab license shall expire on December 31 of the year in which
it is issued. Licenses issued on or after July 1 of any year shall be issued at
one-half the annual license fee herein provided.
   The annual license fee for each taxicab shall be fifty dollars ($50.00), not
to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) per fleet.
(Ord. 1988-171. Passed 11-2-88.)
882.03 LICENSE APPLICATION; ISSUANCE.
   Applications for licenses and certificates shall be filed with the Director
of Safety on forms approved by him. Such applications shall contain a statement
of the name and address of the applicant, the type of business to be
transacted, the kind of equipment, the number of taxicabs to be used, the
conditions of the equipment and such other facts as may be required by the
Director.
   The Director shall investigate and may hold a hearing upon each application
for a license. The Director shall notify the applicant of his findings, whether
they are that the public convenience and necessity do not justify the operation
of the vehicle for which a license is desired, that the public convenience and
necessity do justify the operation of the vehicle for which a license is
desired.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.04 INSURANCE OR OTHER SECURITY.
   No license or certificate shall be issued, nor shall any taxicab be operated
on the streets of the City, until the applicant has filed with the Director of
Safety a casualty insurance policy from an insurance company that is approved
by the Director of Law. Such policy shall indemnify such applicant in the sum
of at least one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) for injury or death to one
person, three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) for injury or death to more
than one person in the same accident, and fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) for
property damage in any one accident, through the operation of the taxicab of
such applicant. Such policy shall further contain a clause obligating the
casualty company to give ten days written notice to the Director of Safety
before $ancellation of such policy.
   In the case of a public vehicle already licensed by a municipality in the
greater Cleveland area and for which a bond, policy or certificate of liability
insurance or a security agreement has been furnished to the municipality
issuing such license, it shall be sufficient for the owner or operator of such
public vehicle to file a copy of such policy or certificate of insurance, bond
of indemnity or security agreement with the Director of Safety, provided,
however, that such policy or certificate of insurance, bond of indemnity or
security agreement shall be subject to the approval of the Director of Safety
and the Director of Law, which approval shall not be given unless the terms of
such policy or certificate, bond of indemnity or security agreement are such as
will protect passengers or other persons or property injured or damaged by the
operation of such public vehicle in the City. Nothing herein contained shall be
deemed to be a waiver of the ten days written notice to the Director of Safety
before cancellation of any such policy or certificate of insurance, indemnity
bond or security agreement, nor a waiver of the right of I the Director of
Safety to order the owner of such public vehicle to replace such policy or
certificate of insurance, bond of indemnity or security agreement.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.05 TAXICAB STANDS.
   The Director of Safety may designate a regular parking space for the
taxicab, and he may prescribe rules for usage of such stand suitable to the
applicant's business and agreeable with the public convenience and welfare.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.06 DISPLAY OF RATES; OVERCHARGING.
   Every taxicab shall display at all times a printed list of the fares and
rates to be charged passengers for transportation. No owner or driver shall
charge any amount in excess of such printed rates except by mutual agreement
between the passenger and the driver entered into before leaving the point of
departure.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.07 AGE LIMIT FOR DRIVERS.
   No person under eighteen years of age shall operate a taxicab on any street
or alley of the City.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.08 SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION OF VEHICLE LICENSE.
   Whenever a licensee fails to make a reasonable or consistent effort to
operate his taxicab for a period of sixty days, the Director of Safety may
either suspend or revoke his license after giving the licensee an opportunity
to show cause why his license should not be suspended or revoked. Such hearing
shall be held by the Director within ten days after such sixty-day period, and
the licensee shall be notified of the time and place of such hearing by
registered mail. Upon failure of the licensee to show cause, the Director shall
revoke or suspend the license, whichever best serves the interests of the
community, and such revocation or suspension shall become effective upon notice
served upon such licensee.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.09 RENEWAL OF VEHICLE LICENSE.
   All owners of taxicabs licensed under this chapter at the completion of the
year for which the license was issued, shall be entitled to a renewal of such
license for each succeeding year, provided that all other requirements of this
chapter have been complied with.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
882.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree and shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty
days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)

884.01 REMOVAL; PERMIT REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   No person shall remove topsoil, loam, sand, gravel, rock, stone, clay, fill
dirt or other similar substance from any land within the City without first
obtaining a permit therefor from the Building Commissioner, but no such permit
shall be issued without the consent of Council. Such application shall be in
writing, giving the name and address of the applicant and the owner of the
property involved, a description of the property, the method of removal to be
employed, the time within which such work is to be commenced and completed, the
depth to which it is proposed that the material be removed and the steps to be
taken towards restoration and ultimate use of the land. The Building
Commissioner may require the applicant to submit topographical maps of the land
before and after such removal.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.02 PERMIT FEE.
   The fee for the permit required by Section
884.01 is an amount equal to twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for each acre foot of
soil or material to be removed in, order to defray the expense of issuing the
permit and inspecting the premises. The Commissioner may issue such permit by
and with the consent of Council if he or she finds that all of the conditions
of this chapter will be, or have been, complied with, and if he or she finds
that no nuisance or hazard to any person or property will be created by such
operation.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.03 BOND.
   Before the issuance of a permit required by Section
884.01, the applicant shall post a bond in an amount to be determined by
Council, which shall not, in any case, be less than five thousand dollars
($5,000), in favor of the City, conditioned upon the performance of the removal
in accordance with this chapter and, the terms of such permit, signed by the
applicant and a good and satisfactory corporate surety.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.04 PERMIT ISSUANCE AND RENEWAL; RELEASE OF BOND.
   The permit shall be issued for a specified period of tune based upon the
applicant's estimated completion date, and the bond provided for in Section
884.03 shall be conditioned upon the completion of the work to be performed
within such specified time. The applicant may, however, obtain a renewal of
such permit from time to time from the Building Commissioner, with the consent
of Council. The bond shall not be released until completion and restoration, as
provided for in the applicant's plans and in this chapter, have been approved
by Council.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.05 WHEN REMOVAL PROHIBITED.
   No removal of topsoil or other materials referred to in Section
884.01 will be permitted if such removal would change or alter natural drainage
from the land affected or result in the collection of stagnant water, excessive
run-off, erosion or flooding of other lands. Within six months from the
completion of such operation, the area affected shall be regraded to contours
and grades as natural and level as possible in order to remove all abrupt
breaks or banks, piles or mounds in the topography, and the affected area shall
be reseeded at the applicant's expense, in accordance with the specifications
of the State Department of Transportation.
   No person who operates an open pit shale or clay mine in any use district
shall strip the overburden within 100 horizontal feet of the centerline of any
road or within 100 horizontal feet of the property line of any property
adjacent to any other property owner. The operator shall place and maintain at
all times adequate fences around the area being mined.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.06 WORKING HOURS; SPILLAGE.
   Bulldozing, loading and dumping Operations, or any other operations creating
any noise, shall be performed only between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m.
from Monday to Saturday, inclusive, and no operation shall be performed on
Sundays or holidays. Trucks or other vehicles shall not be so loaded with
topsoil or other material that results in or causes spilling of soil or
materials on the streets or highways.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
884.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degreeand shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty
days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or Continues.
(Ord. 1986-116. Passed 1-7-87.)
